By Sowmya (Mentee) & Adithya 
(Mentor)
Back Next
Centsible 💵💰

Background
- A personal finance app with multiple 
features 
- Expense Tracking
- Streak Save
- Split Bill
- Mystery Item
- Currency Convertor
Next

Inspiration
Problem:
- Help people understand and track how much they spend.
- Make it easier to manage and organize expenses.
Target Users:
- College students gaining financial independence.
- People who regularly spend money on shared activities (e.g., 
friends going out together).
Solution:
- Show users their transactions clearly.
- Help them split and manage shared expenses easily.
Next

Languages Used
- JavaScript: Used to make the app interactive and respond to 
user actions.
- HTML & CSS: Used to design and style the app’s appearance, 
such as layouts, colors, and buttons.
- Python: Used for the backend, which processes data and 
handles tasks like saving transactions or splitting expenses.
- SQL: Used to manage and store data in a database, such as 
user information and spending history.

Libraries
- React: Helps build the user interface quickly using 
reusable components.
- Firebase: Provides secure login features and stores 
user data safely in the cloud.
- Express: Helps manage server requests and connects 
the app to the database smoothly.

Mentorship Program Takeaways
- Met with my mentor on Zoom once a week — it was nice 
having that regular check-in to stay on track.
- I could always email questions in between meetings.
-  Gave great feedback on my app and helped me think about 
how to organize my code better.
-  They shared helpful resources like The Odin Project to 
strengthen my JavaScript skills.
- Helped me understand tricky coding concepts by breaking 
them down step by step.

Future Plans for Centsible
- Add a receipt upload feature
- Create weekly and monthly spending trackers
- Add more features/components like charts or reminders
- Improve design and usability
- Keep learning and refining the app

Background and Inspiration
● Problem: Lack of awareness and transparency around 
where waste goes after you dispose of it, leading many to 
unintentionally increase excess waste sent to landﬁlls
● Inspired by Arizona State University’s OSCAR waste 
sorting systems around campus, I designed the Waste 
Classiﬁer App to help ASU students and faculty properly 
dispose of their waste 
● Advantage: Easier to use and available all the time and 
everywhere, as compared to limited locations of ASU’s 
OSCAR model
● Aligns with ASU’s goals of making more sustainable and 
environmentally-friendly choices
ASU’s OSCAR Sort

it, including locations on ASU’s campus.

Step 1: Machine Learning Classification Model
● Gathered “New Trash Classiﬁcation” Dataset from Kaggle
● Split Data into 8 Categories: Paper, Plastic, Glass, Cardboard, Metal, Organic, E-Waste, 
Textile, Landﬁll 
● Used Google’s Teachable Machine interface to create a Machine Learning model based on 
Convolutional Neural Network architecture
● Keras library used for deep-learning framework in the ML model due to its easy-to-use 
interface for training neural networks and support of sequential models for stacked layers
● Set Model’s parameter values for optimal accuracy after experimentation
- Epoch: 50 
- Batch size: 16
- Learning rate: 0.001
● Trained and tested AI model for highest accuracy and efﬁciency
Methodology

8
Step 2: Web Application with User Interface
Methodology
● Create web application using Streamlit
- Streamlit chosen as it allowed for an efﬁcient open-source Python framework to 
create an interactive data application for the machine learning model
● Python programming language
● Libraries 
- Tensorﬂow: chosen because it can run the AI/ML models on CPU efﬁciently for creating 
the web application
- Numpy: chosen because it allows for efﬁcient implementation of multi-dimensional 
arrays of images and for mathematical operations in model’s classiﬁcation predictions
- Pillow: chosen because of ease to work with pictures in many formats, including 
transforming and resizing the test and train images for the model

9
Future Plans
In the future, I would like to turn the Waste 
Classiﬁer App from a web application to a mobile 
application to increase ease of use for students and 
faculty. Through the mobile application, users can 
directly take a photo from the app and get instant 
information regarding proper disposal methods and 
locations at ASU, without the extra step of having 
to upload the photos.
A feature I would add to the Waste Classiﬁer 
mobile application is that ability for the program to 
output the closet disposal (recycle, trash, compost, 
etc) bins available to a person via access to the 
person’s location.

culture-bites.text:
CUL TUREBITES
SODA PROJECTPITCH
BY VISHAL LAKSHMI NARAY ANAN

PROBLEM
People feel more “connected” 
digitally but lonelier in real life.
Immigrants and locals rarely 
interact beyond surface-level 
spaces.
Food ,our most natural way to 
connect, has become impersonal.
There’s no space where people can 
meet, share, and belong again.
CULTURE BITES

Culture Bites is a cultural 
exchange platform that uses 
food as the vehicle for 
community engagement.
Users can sign up for intimate 
group dining experiences, 
bonding with new friends over 
home cooked meals.
ABOUT CULTURE BITES

● Culture Bites envisions a world where technology doesn’t just connect screens, 
but connects people again  face to face, through food.
● Our goal is to turn every shared meal into a micro-community  powered by 
transparent systems, local empowerment, and scalable tech infrastructure.
● The platform isn’t just about dining; it’s about engineering empathy at scale.
VISION & OBJECTIVE
CULTURE BITES

THE ECOSYSTEM
GUESTS
Discover authentic food events near 
them.Join shared tables, 
experience cultures ﬁrsthand, and 
leave with more than a meal ,a story.
HOSTS
Open their homes or spaces for 
gatherings.
Create a safe, welcoming 
environment where stories, ﬂavors, 
and friendships grow.
COOKS
Share their culture through 
home-cooked dishes.
Turn recipes into stories that build 
empathy and celebrate identity.
CULTURE BITES

● Guests book and attend dining 
events near them
● Filter by cuisine, date, price, dietary 
preferences
● Guests pay a fee that includes a 
service fee and portion of the 
ingredient cost
Guests gain good food, and exposure to new people and experiences! 
Guests Gain Good Food

● Hosts offer their space to cooks for 
events
● Builds trust, hospitality, and 
community identity through shared 
spaces
● Churches, community centers, 
clubhouses can get more use out of 
their space
● Hosts receive a 25% commission 
per guest
 Not everyone can cook, but they can still participate and beneﬁt
Hosts Turn Homes Into Hubs

● Anyone with cooking skills can 
share their authentic cultural 
knowledge
● Set menus, prices, and schedule 
events
● Partner with hosts or use their own 
space
● Cooks receive a 60% commission 
per guest 
Gives underrepresented communities a way to make a living off their lived experiences!
Cooks share Culture

Features and Functionalities
Event Management System
Comprehensive event lifecycle management:
Event Properties:
● Title, cuisine type, description
● Date, start/end time, location
● Seat capacity and availability
● Host and Cook assignments
● Rich media (multiple images)
Guest Interaction:
● Seat request submission
● Dietary restrictions/notes
● Request status: Pending → 
Approved/Waitlist/Declined
● Real-time availability updates
Collaboration Request System
Two-way marketplace enabling Cooks and Hosts to 
partner:
Request Type | Flow | Status Tracking
Cook → Host | Cook proposes dishes for Host's space | 
Pending → Accepted/Declined
Host → Cook | Host invites Cook for speciﬁc event | 
Pending → Accepted/Declined
Features:
● Proposed dish lists
● Custom messages
● Request history tracking
● Real-time status updates
Multi-Step Proﬁle Wizards
Guided proﬁle creation with validation:
Host Proﬁle Wizard:
1. Space title and description
2. Location and capacity
3. Venue photos (upload or Pexels search)
4. Review and submit
Cook Proﬁle Wizard:
1. Name and origin country
2. Specialties and cuisine types
3. Personal story
4. Cuisine images
5. Review and submit

clarityread.text:
ClarityRead
AI-assisted learning of academic papers.

ClarityRead was inspired by the challenges college students face 
when navigating complex academic research. Academic papers 
often use dense terminology and complicated language, making 
comprehension difﬁcult. Students also lack a way to ask 
questions and get immediate, clarifying responses from the 
authors. ClarityRead aims to bridge that gap.
Project Inspiration:

ClarityRead empowers students to navigate academic papers 
with ease. It uses AI to summarize papers, explain complex 
terminology, and answer questions about the content in real time. 
These features simplify the research process and make academic 
writing more accessible.
The Solution:

Here is a demonstration of how the website can be used in its 
current state:

Backend: Django and MongoDB provide a flexible and easy-to-integrate foundation.Frontend: ReactJS with Tailwind CSS enables clean, responsive UI components and consistent styling.AI Integration: Currently uses the free tier of Gemini for simplicity in early deployment.Technology Choices: Selected to streamline development and accelerate project progress.
The Tech Stack:

Frontend Guidance: Built conﬁdence in ReactJS and Tailwind 
CSS despite limited prior interest in frontend development.
Backend Experience: First time working with MongoDB and 
connecting it to the backend.
AI Integration: Gained hands-on experience incorporating AI 
tools into a full-stack application.
Mentor Support: Helped understand ReactJS syntax nuances 
and guided informed design decisions.
What I’ve Learned:

Expand Content: Increase the number of academic domains, 
subdomains, and total papers available.
Enhance UI: Make the interface more engaging, intuitive, and visually 
consistent.
Improve AI Experience: Ensure AI tools feel seamless, helpful, and 
enhance comprehension throughout the research process.
Add and Improve Features: I have plans to add more paper suggestion 
systems, along with engagement systems for interacting with other 
users, expressing opinions on papers, and more.
Future Plans:

ClarityRead simpliﬁes academic research by making papers 
easier to understand through AI-powered summaries and 
explanations. The project strengthened my full-stack 
development skills, including ReactJS, Tailwind CSS, Django, 
MongoDB, and AI integration. Overall, ClarityRead demonstrates 
how AI can enhance learning and support students in navigating 
complex academic literature.
Summary:

AegisCheck
Uniﬁed AI-Powered Device Security Advisor

The Problem
Too many separate 
tools.
Passwords, 
settings, and 
permissions not 
checked together .
Tools can’t properly 
forecast future 
risks.
Fragmentation Blind Spots No Prediction

● All-in-one security analysis, no 
juggling multiple tools
● Integrated AI risk analyzer (onboard 
neural network + Grok API)
● Predictive insights for future 
vulnerabilities
● Simple, clean interface
The Solution

● OS Security Scan – checks updates, 
security settings, and system integrity
● Password Audit – scans saved 
passwords for breaches, Wi-Fi proﬁles, 
and risky reuse
● Permissions & Autostart Audit – reviews 
app permissions and startup programs
● Predictive AI – onboard neural network + 
Grok API anticipate future vulnerabilities
● Uniﬁed Dashboard – simple interface; 
platform-speciﬁc details hidden unless 
expanded
How it Works

AI Integration
● Onboard Neural Network + 
Grok API integration
● Predicts potential future 
vulnerabilities
● Generates actionable insights 
for OS, passwords, and 
permissions
● Summarizes risk in a simple 
score & grade

● Uniﬁed device security , predictive AI, 
actionable insights
● Continuously learns from your device 
history
● Future expandability: new checks, 
integrations, multi-device support
● Scalable framework for evolving security 
challenges
Conclusion & Future

Mentorship Takeaways
● Gained hands-on experience integrating AI with system 
security checks
● Learned to design a project with real-world impact and 
measurable outcomes
● Understood the importance of structuring code for scalability 
and maintainability
● Improved problem-solving and debugging skills through mentor 
guidance
